OptimizerSentence: With 60 evaluations the median checkpoint fidelity across instances was 1.000 for the exact objective and 0.975 for the counted objective, whose runs used about 614\,400 simulator shots each; the worst counted seed reached 0.201.
RetroSentence: For the two-CZ VQLS circuits every model predicts the measured distributions to within the shot noise (median distance 0.012). For the 104--143 CZ circuits of 5 October the thermal-idle model is closest (median distance 0.070 for HHL and 0.078 for QSVT), whereas for the 223 and 302 CZ circuits of 14 September all gate-local models underpredict the measured error; the parameter-free global-depolarizing model comes closest (predicted TV 0.569 and 0.557 against measured 0.634 and 0.681). No model reproduces the QSVT XZ error, which suggests coherent or crosstalk errors outside all four models.
PreregSentence: Under the thermal-idle-readout model 39 of 39 coherent cells have negative predicted gain. The Nighthawk block, including the mitigation arm, is estimated at 504 QPU seconds.
PreregHHLdevices: On \texttt{ibm\_rensselaer} and \texttt{ibm\_kingston} every gate-local HHL prediction for H4 and H5 is negative and every global-depolarizing prediction positive; on \texttt{ibm\_boston} the depolarizing-readout model also predicts a positive gain ($0.09$ to $0.24$).
CampaignSentence: All 27 planned jobs ran once between 13 and 16 October 2026 (UTC) and were collected. On \texttt{ibm\_rensselaer} the provider calibrations in force were last updated on 13 and 14 October (B1), 15 October (B2) and 16 October (B3), so consecutive blocks are separated by at least one recalibration. B1 and T1 on \texttt{ibm\_kingston} each span two provider calibrations; every job is predicted and analyzed against its own. The jobs were charged 2236 QPU seconds, 71 seconds (3.3\%) above their pre-submission estimates; per job the charge exceeded the estimate by 1.6 to 4.0 seconds.
ConfirmationHHL: The pre-registered decision cells, HHL on H4 and H5, give a processor-dependent answer. On \texttt{ibm\_rensselaer} (321--323 CZ) the gains were $-0.74$, $-0.48$ and $-0.68$ on H4 and $-1.22$, $-1.07$ and $-1.08$ on H5 in B1, B2 and B3; every interval lies below zero. On \texttt{ibm\_kingston} (383--385 CZ) they reached $-0.75$ $[-0.85, -0.64]$ on H4 and $-1.15$ $[-1.34, -0.95]$ on H5. On \texttt{ibm\_boston} (383--385 CZ) they reached $0.14$ $[0.02, 0.27]$ on H4 (the only coherent cell of the campaign with an interval above zero) and $-0.42$ $[-0.57, -0.26]$ on H5.
ConfirmationPredictions: Before any of these runs, the gate-local models had each predicted the sign of the HHL gain for nine of these ten measurements, and the global-depolarizing model for one. For H4 on \texttt{ibm\_boston} the pre-registered gains were $0.70$ (global), $0.24$ (depolarizing-readout) and $-0.08$ (thermal-idle-readout). From the job-start calibration the thermal-idle-readout model predicted $0.14$ for this cell against $-0.34$ to $-0.23$ on \texttt{ibm\_rensselaer} and $-0.32$ on \texttt{ibm\_kingston} for the same instance, so the difference between the processors is already visible in their calibration data. For H5 on the same processor it predicted $0.01$, against the measured $-0.42$.
ConfirmationQSVT: QSVT on the same instances (403--502 CZ) stayed far below input preparation on every processor and block, with $G$ from $-1.46$ to $-0.66$, against pre-registered predictions of $-1.21$ to $-0.34$; 9 of 10 cells fall below all three of their own model predictions.
ConfirmationFidelity: Apart from HHL on \texttt{ibm\_boston} ($F=0.63$ on H4 and $F=0.53$ on H5), the raw fidelities of the coherent H4 and H5 cells lie between $0.19$ and $0.36$, around the value $1/4$ of a maximally mixed two-qubit state, whose inversion gain would be $-0.75$ on H4 and $-1.28$ on H5; these outputs retain little of the prepared state. The intervals of QSVT on H5 in B2 and B3 on \texttt{ibm\_rensselaer} lie entirely below that value, which depolarizing noise alone cannot produce.
ConfirmationVQLS: The frozen VQLS states resolved positive gains in 19 of 38 cells: on H3 in four of five blocks ($0.40$ to $0.67$; $-0.05$ on \texttt{ibm\_kingston}, where the solution-state control also reached only $G=0.01$), on H4 in all five blocks ($0.93$ to $0.96$), on H5 in all five blocks ($0.19$ to $0.28$) and on H6 in all five blocks ($0.52$ to $0.84$). On D0, H1 and H2, where $1-\Fin\le0.042$, no VQLS interval lies above zero.
ConfirmationControls: Input-state controls on H4 and H5 gave $G$ between $-0.07$ and $0.03$ in every block, close to the value $0$ of ideal input preparation, and solution-state controls on all seven instances reached raw fidelity $0.88$ to $1.00$.
ConfirmationMitigation: The dynamical-decoupling and twirling arm changed the raw fidelity of its 7 solver cells by $-0.018$ on average (from $-0.094$ to $0.038$) relative to the raw arm of the same block.
ConfirmationRepro: Across the three \texttt{ibm\_rensselaer} blocks the cell fidelity varied by more than its mean shot-noise half-width for 9 of the 13 coherent cells but for 6 of the 19 shallow cells (VQLS states and controls); the largest standard deviation, $0.21$, belongs to HHL on H2. The decision cells varied by less than their shot-noise intervals: the HHL fidelities on H4 and H5 had standard deviations of $0.057$ and $0.027$ against mean half-widths of $0.091$ and $0.106$.
ConfirmationModels: On every processor the thermal-idle-readout model has the smallest mean absolute fidelity error, both as pre-registered ($0.048$, $0.078$ and $0.074$ on \texttt{ibm\_rensselaer}, \texttt{ibm\_kingston} and \texttt{ibm\_boston}) and from job-start calibrations ($0.056$, $0.086$ and $0.066$), with Spearman rank correlations of $0.93$ to $0.96$; only 28 to 41\% of its job-start predictions fall inside the measured intervals. Every model is optimistic on average: the observed minus predicted job-start fidelity ranges from $-0.295$ (logical-ideal) to $-0.053$ (thermal-idle-readout).
ConfirmationSentence: The five blocks comprise 167 analyzed cells in 27 jobs, 7 of them in the mitigation arm (Table~\ref{tab:hardware}, Fig.~\ref{fig:hardware}). A raw inversion-gain interval lies entirely above zero for 1 of the 69 coherent cells and for 19 of the 38 VQLS cells, none of them in the mitigation arm.
AbstractConfirmation: In 27 jobs (three blocks on \texttt{ibm\_rensselaer} and one on each of \texttt{ibm\_kingston} and \texttt{ibm\_boston}), the HHL measurements pre-registered as decisive stayed below input preparation on \texttt{ibm\_rensselaer} in all three blocks and on \texttt{ibm\_kingston}, whereas on \texttt{ibm\_boston} a circuit with 385 controlled-Z gates reached $G=0.14$ (95\% interval $0.02$ to $0.27$) on the star instance, the only one of 69 coherent-solver measurements resolved above zero; each gate-local calibration model had predicted the sign of nine of the ten decisive measurements, a global-depolarizing model only one. Frozen variational states resolved positive gains in 19 of 38 measurements, reflecting faithful preparation of classically trained states.
ConclusionConfirmation: Across five blocks on three processors, verified coherent solvers fell below input preparation on every inversion-sensitive cell except HHL on H4 on \texttt{ibm\_boston}, $G=0.14$ $[0.02, 0.27]$, a result that rests on one job under one calibration and that the thermal-idle-readout model anticipated from the job-start calibration. The frozen VQLS states, which need only a few CZ gates, resolved positive gains in 19 of 38 cells; they demonstrate faithful preparation of classically trained states, not hardware solving. Repeating the resolved cell under independent calibrations is the most informative next experiment, and the same protocol certifies its outcome.
